title: Re: UX: Immediate Intent vs. Optimistic Update...
text:
I've grown tired of explaining to frontend devs why "optimistic updates" are harmful and why immediate intent is always better, so I invested a couple hours of my life and some amount of Claude tokens to explain this once and for all.

Let's not make software bad by design, let's make good reliable software we can trust.

P.S. maybe I'm wrong? Challenge me in the GitHub issues!

title: Re: I'm Scared of AI...
text:
I don't know if this is good advice as the world is moving so fast, but I am still able to get those good "I accomplished something" chemicals by being much more ambitious in the tasks I take on with AI.

For example, I have a side business selling jewelry on the internet. Every week, I get a batch of rings from my casting house. I weigh them, measure the size and width, and take a photo or two. Recently with Claude fable 5.2 I tasked it with building me a contraption to do all of this with one click and get it into my database. We worked back on forth and came up with a design that I should be able to assemble and test soon. This is something I could have designed and built over many many days/weeks of work, but instead it took 1.

Maybe I am "lucky" that I get feelings of accomplishment from that and maybe I shouldn't actually feel accomplished. But I am getting a genuinely useful device and having fun along the way so I think its alright.
